title: Healy, Helen Morgan, Wallace Beery and the improved shows
summary: Thomas recalls producer Healy's celebrity Sundays, a drunk Helen Morgan, Wallace Beery's ovation, and getting Harold Arlen to write full show music.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And then they had this guy, Healy, he was a big shot... See, he got credit for producing the show. But Clarence Robertson and all them other guys produced the show. But he got credit for overseeing it, and he was the producer. And he knew everybody. He used to get more celebrities up there and Sunday night. And I remember this one girl; let's see if I can think of her name now... Helen Morgan. She was up there more than anybody else. I remember her in her days when she was...uh...drank a lot of whiskey. Sometimes she'd be so drunk she couldn't hardly... she couldn't hardly walk out on that floor. And a lot of times she was going to sit on top of the piano, because that's the way singers used to sing anyhow... But she could
sing. She just had that talent.

And he had... I remember at the Uptown Cotton Club, Wallace Beery came in. And he just did a show, a big movie -- and the house came down! They used to have that Sunday night up at the Cotton Club. And all the big entertainers, when they'd come in town, they'd come to the Cotton Club uptown. Because it was big. And Wallace Beery, he got a big hand when he stood up, and all he said, "Oh..." He got such a big ovation, and he said, "Oh, gee," -- the same thing he used to say in the pictures. And the house broke down again.

They protected us, boy. They loved that band. But see, we improved the shows at the Cotton Club. Now, all respects to Duke Ellington. See, Duke Ellington... It was hard for us when we into the show, because he did a lot of his tunes in the show, and we had to get to the spot where we had to play for the dancers... We didn't have none of their music. So when Harold Arlen started writing the show, we made him write the whole show all the way down. So when we went downtown, we carried that thing, too. They had the whole...just nothing but the show music. And it made a difference. And we played that gig...
